results.reason: Issue 1 identifies the five-year auto-renewal and the 270/240-day notice requirement under §2.2. It calls this a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for another five years.

Issue 4 identifies that §3.1 covers all glass and PET containers for any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber-glass, beer-only, U.S./Canada scope and treats Harrowgate as bound by the executed text ('now contractually barred').
Issue 2 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 per Recital C and that the §5.4 objection deadline was September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 3 explains that the Amendment replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It states recall and personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 6 identifies new §14.4 allowing assignment without consent to Affiliates and successors, and mentions a 'competitor's affiliate' as a risk. It never explains that Harrowgate remains bound by the §14.3 consent requirement, so the one-sided nature of the restriction is not addressed.
The response never mentions §15.2 or the rule that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
It states the cap equals the fees paid in the six months before the claim arose (§11.1).
It is a memo to [Partner] with numbered issues. Each issue gives the document and section ('Where') and a recommended fix.
It proposes specific contract language, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1, a revised §2.2 renewal clause and a revised §14.4.
The response treats the objection window as closed and the increase as deemed accepted.
The response treats §3.1 as binding and recommends amending it; it does not say the term sheet's scope governs.
